body: I notice the old oak swaying gently under its own weight but also feeling an immense pressure from the white, plastic tape. It seems to be marking time, its trunk stark against the gray sky. My heart races as I remember how the trees were once so intertwined with life, their branches dancing together like dancers at twilight. Now they're prisoners of a man-made measure, each one marked with a different year, their spirits dulled by the constant surveillance.
